utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84bis-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Madam Registrar. Could we have the appearances for the day, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, Paul Rogers appearing for the Prosecution, together with Ms. Priya Gopalan and our case manager today, Mr. Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Rogers. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Ben Emmerson for Ramush Haradinaj together with Rodney Dixon, Annie O'Reilly, and Andrew Strong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Emmerson. For Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Gregor Guy-Smith and on behalf of Mr. Balaj with Ms. Rohan and Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Guy-Smith. And for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Richard Harvey, together with Paul Troop, Sophie Rigney, Luke Boenisch, and Ms. Rudina Jasini for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we've reached the stage where Mr. Kabashi is due to be called. As I have indicated to the Chamber and all the parties, Mr. Karnavas spoke to me after the first appearance of Mr. Kabashi today in the contempt matter, and instead of saying what he told me, might I invite him to come into the courtroom to address Your Honours directly on the matters that he wishes to raise relating to his views about whether his client should be testifying this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I have been speaking for some time without a microphone. Can I repeat myself. I was saying it might not be necessary to call him in to come and give an explanation. Let's first hear what the other parties have to say, and I'm asking Mr. Emmerson to please start.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure whether you're asking me to respond to the request that the matter be postponed until Monday at this stage, but obviously I have not heard the request articulated or the reasons for it. I would have thought, respectfully, it might be an idea to have Mr. Karnavas into court just to explain the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I thought Mr. Rogers indicated that he sent a message to everybody --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, no, I'm sorry, I've seen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- about what happened, and therefore I would have expected that you might be having a position --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I've seen Mr. Rogers' letter. Obviously he's conveying what it was that Mr. Karnavas had to say. I apprehended that Your Honours might wish to hear Mr. Karnavas briefly, he's just outside the courtroom to explain the position. I can tell you now that assuming what he says is effectively the same as what Mr. Rogers has said in his letter, we will be taking a neutral position and leaving it to the Tribunal to decide how to approach the matter. I understand that Mr. Kabashi is here in the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your position, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Based on the representations that were made in Mr. Rogers' e-mail earlier today, coupled with the representations that I saw Mr. Karnavas make over the internet, or whatever you call it, whatever you call this newfangled --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Over the movie.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Over the movie. My position is two-fold. I recognise the relationship between a lawyer and the client and I recognise the importance of human decency, and I am willing to accede to Mr. Karnavas' request if it remains what I believe it to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I haven't seen the moving-picture image, but I have spoken with Mr. Karnavas directly and I do understand his position in respect of his client and I leave the matter respectfully in the hands of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks for the positions that we got from the parties. May Mr. Karnavas please be brought in just for a complete record. Indeed, please do. Welcome, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, good afternoon, Your Honours, and good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, Mr. -- you're coming here at the invitation of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Prosecution has indicated that you have something to tell the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: About your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. I did inform the Defence yesterday, it was -- that most likely my client would not be able to testify today because of him being caught in this Dutch system which nobody seemed to know, at least on the Netherlands' side, you know, what to do until yesterday afternoon. And because I was not able to meet with my client to at least discuss his testimony and to get him mentally prepared for the Court, I informed them that in all likelihood it would be on Monday. Today I met with my client because we had a hearing. I've discussed the matter with Mr. Kabashi about testifying. It was his wish that he meet with me to discuss his testimony, particularly in light of the fact that he has these counts pending and his performance in this particular court may impact how that situation will be resolved or any potential future situations that may arise in this courtroom. And I did inform Mr. -- Judge Orie, in fact, that I would be bringing to this Trial Chamber's attention the fact that he is not in the shape -- he is psychologically not capable and he's physically exhausted, physically exhausted. And frankly, I think it would be a miscarriage of justice to force him to testify today, given that he hasn't slept in the last couple of days, he hasn't had access to his lawyer, and that no one will be prejudiced if he testifies on Monday. I was scheduled to meet with him between 1.00 and 4.00 this afternoon at the UNDU. Regrettably, that now has changed. Efforts have been made by all there for me to meet with him later this evening, and I'm now also making efforts to see whether the UNDU would allow me to meet with him tomorrow, which is slightly unusual, but I'm hopeful that between OLAD and perhaps the Trial Chamber the UNDU would allow me to meet with Mr. Kabashi so that Monday morning, 9.00, he's here and he's ready and able to give evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Karnavas. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't expect anybody wants to cross-examine Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I -- well, as a matter of fact, Your Honour ... No, but I would make one brief comment, which is as follows, which is to the extent that the Chamber can be of any assistance to Mr. Karnavas in terms of the relationship that he has with the Detention Unit, UNDU, for a Saturday visit, I would strongly encourage that so that we don't run into a problem next week of him not having had the opportunity to meet with Mr. Kabashi because sometimes people are very jealous about the way they treat their weekends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that, Mr. Guy-Smith, and I'm sure Mr. Karnavas is perfectly capable to make appropriate representations to any relevant authorities for further assistance if he does need any. Thank you so much. That's -- that being that, then I suppose we accept what has been said and we'll stand adjourned to Monday - are we sitting in the morning or the afternoon, in the morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we rise there are just a few small housekeeping matters that Ms. Gopalan can deal with, a number of small oral applications that my learned friends have been notified we would make. So perhaps she can make those and we can try to tidy away some loose ends and feel we have achieved something perhaps in the course of this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In that event, Mr. Karnavas, you are excused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome. Yes, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'm here to make an oral application for the admission of the evidence of three witnesses who are scheduled to testify in the remaining sitting period, it's an oral application for the admission of their evidence in written form into the trial record. The first one is Witness 79. She's scheduled to testify sometime next week. We have been in e-mail contact with the Defence and they do not require her -- for her to attend for cross-examination. If Your Honours recall, this witness was mentioned in your decision dated 22nd of July and you had asked for her to appear for cross-examination; however, the parties are in agreement that she does not require to attend for cross-examination. So I ask that her written statement be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ma'am, you said her written statement. Is it 92 bis? 92 ter?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: It's a 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Can we --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I could read out the 65 ter number, if it pleases Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe for the Registrar's sake, yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The 65 ter number is 03042.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, moving on to the remaining witnesses, there are two of theme Mijat and Dragoslav Stojanovic. We have also been in contact with the Defence about the two of them, and all three Defence teams have agreed that these witnesses will not be required to attend to give additional testimony. And so this is an oral application for the admission of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And they are also 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: They are also 92 bis, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Those three witnesses, they testified in the first trial I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Two of them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Two of them, two of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Two of them did, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And did they testify -- was that a viva voce testimony?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And the third one?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And the third one, as I recall, there was a written statement, but that was not part of the initial trial record.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can assist, I can clarify that that statement -- there was an application made under 92 bis to have it admitted, but it wasn't admitted by the previous Trial Chamber. So it wasn't on the record. So as things stand we're only talking about a statement for that witness. There was no testimony. And as we've indicated in our e-mail, there's no objection to that statement. But with regards the other two witnesses, they both did give testimony and were cross-examined and there are associated exhibits with their testimony as well. And there's no objection to their previous statements but in addition to that their previous testimony, including the cross-examination and all the associated exhibits, being admitted into evidences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, what I was proposing to do in relation to the two witnesses, Mijat and Dragoslav Stojanovic was to circulate to the Defence a complete list of the testimony and the associated exhibits so that the parties may -- that they may view the material and then we would seek the admission of all that material into evidence based on the agreement of the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, Madam Gopalan, if I understand Mr. Dixon correctly, it looks like they've had sight of all that material, that's why he's asking -- he's saying that all that material can be -- there's no objection to all that material being tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: There isn't any objection, but we should just be sure what material we are talking about and ensure that all the associated exhibits, both as introduced by the Prosecution and the Defence are part of that category of material. So if we could have an opportunity with the Prosecution just to confirm that and then that material could all be conveyed to the Trial Chamber for admission by agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. It does seem as if that -- your application is a little premature with respect to those two because it doesn't look like they're -- the parties are at ad idem as to what actually should go in just yet, not that there is an objection, but just that they want to make sure. So if you can sort that out so by the time you make that application you are able to tender those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And with respect to the statement -- I recognise you, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And with respect to the statement, the other witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That one you seek to tender it now?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I seek the admission of that statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I seek to tender it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. With respect to that, Mr. Dixon or Mr. Emmerson, what is the response to that? Can you confirm the [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: As we've indicated in our previous e-mails, there's no objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: -- to that statement being admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With regard to the statement, there's no objection to its admission. With regard to the two witnesses who have testified, in terms of the body of information that is going to be presented to the Chamber, I trust that information includes a verbatim copy of the video testimony of their testimony so that the Chamber is in a position if they wish to, to have that information available for determining such things as the way they looked, how they responded, since there will be issues with regard to demeanour, obviously credibility and reliability of their testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Given that the parties are going to go through what has to go in, I guess you will raise that at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am, but I am putting down a marker because I -- it's coming up and I think it's an important thing that the Chamber has in its mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I adopt what Mr. Guy-Smith just said, but in addition to that I say we have no objection, as we've already indicated to the Prosecution, to the testimony of Witness 79 going in for what little use it may be to the Trial Chamber because it is very substantially hearsay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The 65 ter number you gave, was it in respect to the one statement that you want --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- to tender. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about that. Okay, then the statement is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I request that it's admitted under seal since it pertains to a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, it's admitted under seal. Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the statement will be Exhibit P1 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, with -- since we are early in these proceedings, with regard to those exhibits that are admitted under seal, where there has been some protection order which the Defence is not privy to the reasons for that protection, we may at some point wish to revisit whether or not it is appropriate for certain documents to be placed under seal in these proceedings. And I'm raising the point now because I think it's a point that's going to come up in the future again with regard to other statements or other testimony that may take that same form, that being the statement of somebody who is at this point been a protected witness and that protection has been given to them in the absence of the Defence having information with regard to why that protection was given. And by that I'm talking about the factual -- the factual information that was presented to the Chamber ex parte. Once again, I'm only raising it -- I'm not at this point asking that anything be done, but I'm raising the issue because I think it's an issue that could become crystallised in the relatively near future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Noted, Mr. Guy-Smith. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, nothing more on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: But Mr. Rogers, however, would like to address the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, forgive me, I'd mean to raise this earlier. It's about the guide-lines that Your Honours were going to issue, and it occurred to me that we didn't have a finalised version of the guide-lines. And as we are approaching the first stage at which cross-examination will take place, it would be helpful if the Court could today issue its finalised version of the guide-lines relating to when the Defence must disclose to us the documents that they intend to rely upon for the purpose of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber is acutely aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And is desperately trying to get it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I'm sure it is, Your Honour. I just was conscious that today was, in fact, the first day and we hadn't quite bottomed that one out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Perhaps the sooner we get out of here, the sooner it might be attended to. Any others, any party? Mr. Emmerson? Mr. Guy-Smith? Mr. Harvey? Okay. Thank you so much. Then we stand adjourned until Monday, 9.00, in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of August, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.42 p.m.,
